symbols.name: createAIChatStream
signatures: (adapter: AIChatAdapter, request: AIChatRequest, options?: AIChatStreamOptions | undefined): ReadableStream<any>
symbols.summary:
Shared send lifecycle for HTTP, custom and SDK consumers. Snapshots the request
before returning, starts lazily on demand, requires finish followed by EOF,
rejects events after finish, and forwards abort to the adapter even during a read.
Cancellation settles promptly; an adapter must honor its signal to release I/O.
Iterator cleanup is requested, but never awaited behind an uncooperative next().
No storage, retry, resumption, tool execution or browser/SDK dependency.

tags.name: param
tags.text: adapter - Host-supplied transport whose iterator must honor cancellation and release its network resources.

tags.name: param
tags.text: request - Conversation request snapshotted before demand for createAIChatStream, or on first iteration for streamAIChat.

tags.name: param
tags.text: options - Optional serialized-event character budget; defaults to {} and maxResponseChars 1000000 (maximum 10000000).

tags.name: returns
tags.text: A lazy ReadableStream; consume or cancel it to release the adapter iterator.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: Throws/rejects invalid configuration/history, aborts, invalid events, response limits or EOF without finish; events after finish also fail.

tags.name: example

symbols.name: createActionToolBridge
signatures: (registry: ActionRegistry, options: ActionToolBridgeOptions): ActionToolBridge
symbols.summary: Creates an explicitly scoped, provider-neutral bridge to a screen registry.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Tool schemas are application-owned, synchronous JSON Schema draft-07 or 2020-12.
Schemas are compiled on construction using the existing Ajv adapter with coercion,
defaults and property removal disabled. The registered action validator still runs.
No schema, handler, permission or output type is inferred from a TypeScript type.
Only mapOutput results are returned; registry metadata, errors and causes stay local.
The bridge reads the current registration at call time and rejects results if that
action was replaced during execution. Context lifetime checks are owned by the registry.
Duplicate call IDs (including failed calls) are rejected for this bridge's lifetime.
This is local retry protection, not durable idempotency or server authorization.
JSON schemas, arguments and projected outputs must be plain finite JSON data, at most
64 levels deep, 10000 nodes and 1000000 serialized characters per value.
Creating a bridge does not expose data externally or contact an AI service.

tags.name: param
tags.text: registry - Application registry whose current registrations are checked at each call.

tags.name: param
tags.text: options - Explicit tool bindings and optional positive safe-integer maxCalls (default 1000).

tags.name: returns
tags.text: An in-memory bridge with list/execute/close; close suppresses future/in-flight results without undoing effects.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: Throws invalid/duplicate names, invalid call limits/bindings or schema/snapshot compilation errors.

tags.name: example

Do not modify schemas after compilation; provide a new schema object instead.
The returned ajv instance corresponds to the default draft. Specify draft explicitly when using addSchema/addKeyword.
The default path disables type coercion and does not insert defaults or remove
keys. Explicit ajvOptions can enable input mutation. Unknown x-* keywords are
not business validation rules merely because strict mode is disabled.
Compilation/configuration failures throw; invalid data returns valid: false.
Runtime compilation requires a host that permits AJV's generated functions.
Omitted options default to {}; draft-07, no explicit locale, and noncoercing data validation are used.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: Throws Ajv configuration/format-registration failures during construction; later schema compilation failures propagate from the returned validator.

symbols.name: createExecutionSession
signatures: (options?: { readonly historyLimit?: number | undefined; } | undefined): ExecutionSession
symbols.summary:
Creates a framework-independent execution session (default history limit 50, max 1000).
One operation runs at a time. cancel changes status to cancelling and aborts its signal;
it does not race the promise or unlock a handler that ignores cancellation. A handler
resolving after cancellation is recorded as succeeded with cancelRequested=true.
Only an AbortError after a cancellation request is recorded as cancelled. Other errors
remain failures. Late progress updates are ignored. Observers cannot break execution.

History contains bounded labels/progress only, not inputs, results or exception details.
It is transient UI state, not an audit log or durable deduplication. Applications must
handle server authorization, idempotency and uncertain commit outcomes themselves.

tags.name: param
tags.text: options - Optional historyLimit configuration; defaults to {} and historyLimit 50.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: A single-flight in-memory session; the host must close it when no longer needed.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: Throws when historyLimit is not an integer from 1 to 1000.

symbols.name: createGenerativeUIContract
signatures: (components: {}): GenerativeUIContract
symbols.summary: Builds a provider-neutral draft-07 response schema from explicit component definitions.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Up to 32 unique type names, each with an inline object-root dataSchema. References,
IDs, anchors, dialect declarations and async schemas are rejected (including nested
reserved keys); this prevents reference rebasing and mixed-dialect ambiguity when
schemas are composed. No network loading occurs. Schemas are snapshotted/frozen and
compiled immediately using the existing Ajv adapter with coercion/defaults/removal
disabled. Invalid schemas throw configuration errors.
Exported schema describes structural constraints; runtime validation additionally
enforces unique block IDs and JSON size/depth limits. Custom business validators and
authorization still belong to the app. Provider-specific schema subsets may require
an application adapter; this function never contacts an AI service.

tags.name: param
tags.text: components - At most 32 uniquely named component schemas, each inline synchronous draft-07 with an object root.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Frozen composed schema, component snapshots and local runtime validation helpers.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: Throws duplicate/invalid names, too many components, forbidden reference/dialect keys, non-JSON snapshots or Ajv schema errors.

signatures: (input: unknown): GenerativeUIDocumentResult
symbols.summary: Validates and snapshots a fully assembled UI document without a UI dependency.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Requires version 1, a document ID, and at most 32 flat blocks with unique IDs.
Blocks have exactly id/type/data; the envelope has exactly version/id/blocks.
Data must be an object. Component names match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63}`.
All values must be plain finite JSON data: no accessors, functions, cycles,
sparse arrays, class instances or undefined. Limits: 64 nesting levels,
10000 nodes and 1000000 serialized characters for the entire document.
The successful result is cloned and recursively frozen; caller input is untouched.
This validates structure, not business data or authorization. Unknown component
names are allowed here and handled by the application's explicit UI registry.
Parse provider JSON and assemble streaming fragments before calling this function.

tags.text: input - Fully assembled untrusted JSON document, after provider JSON parsing/fragment assembly.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: A detached frozen version-1 document or fixed INVALID_DOCUMENT failure; unknown component names are allowed at this envelope layer.

symbols.name: createExecutionSession
signatures: (options?: { readonly historyLimit?: number | undefined; } | undefined): ExecutionSession
symbols.summary:
Creates a framework-independent execution session (default history limit 50, max 1000).
One operation runs at a time. cancel changes status to cancelling and aborts its signal;
it does not race the promise or unlock a handler that ignores cancellation. A handler
resolving after cancellation is recorded as succeeded with cancelRequested=true.
Only an AbortError after a cancellation request is recorded as cancelled. Other errors
remain failures. Late progress updates are ignored. Observers cannot break execution.

History contains bounded labels/progress only, not inputs, results or exception details.
It is transient UI state, not an audit log or durable deduplication. Applications must
handle server authorization, idempotency and uncertain commit outcomes themselves.

tags.name: param
tags.text: options - Optional historyLimit configuration; defaults to {} and historyLimit 50.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: A single-flight in-memory session; the host must close it when no longer needed.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: Throws when historyLimit is not an integer from 1 to 1000.

symbols.name: createActionToolBridge
signatures: (registry: ActionRegistry, options: ActionToolBridgeOptions): ActionToolBridge
symbols.summary: Creates an explicitly scoped, provider-neutral bridge to a screen registry.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Tool schemas are application-owned, synchronous JSON Schema draft-07 or 2020-12.
Schemas are compiled on construction using the existing Ajv adapter with coercion,
defaults and property removal disabled. The registered action validator still runs.
No schema, handler, permission or output type is inferred from a TypeScript type.
Only mapOutput results are returned; registry metadata, errors and causes stay local.
The bridge reads the current registration at call time and rejects results if that
action was replaced during execution. Context lifetime checks are owned by the registry.
Duplicate call IDs (including failed calls) are rejected for this bridge's lifetime.
This is local retry protection, not durable idempotency or server authorization.
JSON schemas, arguments and projected outputs must be plain finite JSON data, at most
64 levels deep, 10000 nodes and 1000000 serialized characters per value.
Creating a bridge does not expose data externally or contact an AI service.

tags.name: param
tags.text: registry - Application registry whose current registrations are checked at each call.

tags.name: param
tags.text: options - Explicit tool bindings and optional positive safe-integer maxCalls (default 1000).

tags.name: returns
tags.text: An in-memory bridge with list/execute/close; close suppresses future/in-flight results without undoing effects.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: Throws invalid/duplicate names, invalid call limits/bindings or schema/snapshot compilation errors.

symbols.name: createAIChatStream
signatures: (adapter: AIChatAdapter, request: AIChatRequest, options?: AIChatStreamOptions | undefined): ReadableStream<any>
symbols.summary:
Shared send lifecycle for HTTP, custom and SDK consumers. Snapshots the request
before returning, starts lazily on demand, requires finish followed by EOF,
rejects events after finish, and forwards abort to the adapter even during a read.
Cancellation settles promptly; an adapter must honor its signal to release I/O.
Iterator cleanup is requested, but never awaited behind an uncooperative next().
No storage, retry, resumption, tool execution or browser/SDK dependency.

tags.name: param
tags.text: adapter - Host-supplied transport whose iterator must honor cancellation and release its network resources.

tags.name: param
tags.text: request - Conversation request snapshotted before demand for createAIChatStream, or on first iteration for streamAIChat.

tags.name: param
tags.text: options - Optional serialized-event character budget; defaults to {} and maxResponseChars 1000000 (maximum 10000000).

tags.name: returns
tags.text: A lazy ReadableStream; consume or cancel it to release the adapter iterator.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: Throws/rejects invalid configuration/history, aborts, invalid events, response limits or EOF without finish; events after finish also fail.

tags.name: example

symbols.name: createGenerativeUIContract
signatures: (components: {}): GenerativeUIContract
symbols.summary: Builds a provider-neutral draft-07 response schema from explicit component definitions.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Up to 32 unique type names, each with an inline object-root dataSchema. References,
IDs, anchors, dialect declarations and async schemas are rejected (including nested
reserved keys); this prevents reference rebasing and mixed-dialect ambiguity when
schemas are composed. No network loading occurs. Schemas are snapshotted/frozen and
compiled immediately using the existing Ajv adapter with coercion/defaults/removal
disabled. Invalid schemas throw configuration errors.
Exported schema describes structural constraints; runtime validation additionally
enforces unique block IDs and JSON size/depth limits. Custom business validators and
authorization still belong to the app. Provider-specific schema subsets may require
an application adapter; this function never contacts an AI service.

tags.name: param
tags.text: components - At most 32 uniquely named component schemas, each inline synchronous draft-07 with an object root.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Frozen composed schema, component snapshots and local runtime validation helpers.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: Throws duplicate/invalid names, too many components, forbidden reference/dialect keys, non-JSON snapshots or Ajv schema errors.

tags.name: example

symbols.name: validateGenerativeUIDocument
signatures: (input: unknown): GenerativeUIDocumentResult
symbols.summary: Validates and snapshots a fully assembled UI document without a UI dependency.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Requires version 1, a document ID, and at most 32 flat blocks with unique IDs.
Blocks have exactly id/type/data; the envelope has exactly version/id/blocks.
Data must be an object. Component names match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63}`.
All values must be plain finite JSON data: no accessors, functions, cycles,
sparse arrays, class instances or undefined. Limits: 64 nesting levels,
10000 nodes and 1000000 serialized characters for the entire document.
The successful result is cloned and recursively frozen; caller input is untouched.
This validates structure, not business data or authorization. Unknown component
names are allowed here and handled by the application's explicit UI registry.
Parse provider JSON and assemble streaming fragments before calling this function.

tags.name: param
tags.text: input - Fully assembled untrusted JSON document, after provider JSON parsing/fragment assembly.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: A detached frozen version-1 document or fixed INVALID_DOCUMENT failure; unknown component names are allowed at this envelope layer.

tags.name: example

signatures: <TRecord extends Record<string, any> = Record<string, any>>(entries: {}, validateCandidate?: ProposalBatchValidator<TRecord> | undefined): PreparedProposalBatch<TRecord>
symbols.summary:
Prepares every selected record before a multi-record apply starts.
Reuses single-proposal decisions, before/version checks and candidate validation.
Duplicate proposal IDs anywhere and duplicate selected target IDs fail closed.
Every selected proposal needs all fields decided and at least one accepted change.
Exclude all-rejected proposals explicitly. Empty selection is not executable.

Pass proposals already validated with validateProposalInput. This is not an external
input parser, cross-record business validator, database transaction or authorization
boundary. Payload candidates are shallow immutable snapshots, like buildApplyPayload.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Frozen preflight diagnostics and shallow immutable payload candidates; any issue empties the payload list, and empty selection cannot apply.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Automatically selects draft-07/2020-12 based on $schema; compiled functions are not shared across instances.
Do not modify schemas after compilation; provide a new schema object instead.
The returned ajv instance corresponds to the default draft. Specify draft explicitly when using addSchema/addKeyword.
The default path disables type coercion and does not insert defaults or remove
keys. Explicit ajvOptions can enable input mutation. Unknown x-* keywords are
not business validation rules merely because strict mode is disabled.
Compilation/configuration failures throw; invalid data returns valid: false.
Runtime compilation requires a host that permits AJV's generated functions.
Omitted options default to {}; draft-07, no explicit locale, and noncoercing data validation are used.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: Throws Ajv configuration/format-registration failures during construction; later schema compilation failures propagate from the returned validator.

symbols.name: addDays
signatures: (date: any, days: number): Date
symbols.summary: Adds multiples of a fixed 24-hour duration to an instant.

tags.name: param
tags.text: date - Date or runtime-parseable string providing the starting instant.

tags.name: param
tags.text: days - Number of 86,400,000-millisecond periods to add; negative and fractional values are accepted.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: A new Date from elapsed-millisecond arithmetic; invalid/non-finite inputs produce an invalid Date.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text: This does not preserve wall-clock time across daylight-saving transitions and is not a civil-calendar day operation.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
```ts
import { addDays } from '@alneas/appkit-core/data/date-utils';
console.log(addDays('2024-01-15T00:00:00Z', 7).toISOString()); // '2024-01-22T00:00:00.000Z'
```

symbols.summary:
Convert form values, separately from JSON Schema validation. Never adds defaults,
resolves $ref, selects composition branches, or coerces booleans/dates/null values.

Mismatched object/array values and unconvertible strings are retained for validation.
Walks only own declared properties, prefixItems and items; unknown properties survive.
Does not mutate inputs. Throws beyond depth 64 or 10,000 visited values (including cycles).

signatures: (date1: any, date2: any, timeZone?: string | undefined): 0 | 1 | -1

symbols.name: compareTimes
signatures: (time1: string, time2: string): 0 | 1 | -1
symbols.summary: Compares two colon-separated clock strings after converting their first two fields to numbers.

tags.name: param
tags.text: time1 - First clock string, conventionally HH:mm.

tags.name: param
tags.text: time2 - Second clock string, conventionally HH:mm.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Minus one, one or zero for lower, higher or equal computed minute totals. Malformed fields can yield NaN and therefore compare as zero.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text: This is not a range/format validator. Seconds and additional fields are ignored; negative or out-of-range numeric fields are not rejected.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
```ts
import { compareTimes } from '@alneas/appkit-core/data/date-utils';
console.log(compareTimes('09:00', '14:30')); // -1
console.log(compareTimes('invalid', '14:30')); // 0; validate before comparing.
```

symbols.name: createAjvValidator
signatures: (options?: AjvValidatorOptions | undefined): ((schema: object, data: unknown, overrides?: any) => { valid: boolean; errors: {}; rawErrors?: {} | undefined; }) & { ajv: any; }
symbols.summary: Creates a validator using Ajv.

tags.name: param
tags.text: options - Validation options.

tags.name: param
tags.text: options.locale - Error message locale ('ja' | 'en'). If omitted, Ajv default messages are used.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Validation execution function.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Automatically selects draft-07/2020-12 based on $schema; compiled functions are not shared across instances.
Do not mutate the schema object after compilation; pass a new object instead.
The returned `ajv` property is the instance for the default draft. When using addSchema/addKeyword, specify the draft explicitly.
The default path disables type coercion and does not insert defaults or remove
keys. Explicit ajvOptions can enable input mutation. Unknown x-* keywords are
not business validation rules merely because strict mode is disabled.
Compilation/configuration failures throw; invalid data returns valid: false.
Runtime compilation requires a host that permits AJV's generated functions.

symbols.name: generateZodSchema
signatures: (schema: JSONSchema): ZodObject<Readonly<{ [k: string]: $ZodType<unknown, unknown, $ZodTypeInternals<unknown, unknown>>; }>, $strip>
symbols.summary:
Generates a Zod validation schema from a JSONSchema.

Produces appropriate Zod validators according to property type/format,
applying implemented JSON Schema constraints and supported x-zod extensions.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Partial conversion, not a JSON Schema evaluator. additionalProperties, type
unions and positive multipleOf are supported. Exclusive bounds, composition,
references and advanced array constraints are not generally preserved. format: date only
checks string type. Use createAjvValidator at the authoritative JSON boundary.
Only implemented x-zod options take effect; declarations do not imply support.
Root/nested required entries are checked even without properties declarations;
enum applies at the root as well as to nested values.
Declared/required __proto__ properties are rejected at conversion time.

tags.name: param
tags.text: schema - JSONSchema schema

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Zod object schema

tags.name: example

symbols.name: generateZodSchemaCode
signatures: (schema: JSONSchema): string
symbols.summary: Serializes a JSON Schema into a module that calls generateZodSchema at runtime.

tags.name: param
tags.text:
schema - JSON-serializable schema; title, then x-db.tableName, then
"unnamed" supplies the export-name prefix. Non-identifier characters become
underscores and a leading digit receives an underscore prefix.

tags.name: returns
tags.text:
Module source importing generateZodSchema from "./compiler.js" and exporting
the named schema by passing JSON.parse of the serialized input to that helper.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: Throws if JSON serialization fails, for example for cyclic input or BigInt.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
The output is not a standalone z.object expression and this function does not
validate or compile the schema. Evaluating the emitted module runs the helper
and can raise its schema-conversion errors. Provide a sibling compiler module
exporting generateZodSchema and a resolver that supports the emitted extensionless
import; native Node.js ESM does not resolve that import without adjustment.
The runtime helper uses Zod, which is a Core dependency.

tags.name: example

symbols.summary: Extracts the hour/minute fields of an instant in a selected timezone and converts them to a minute count.

tags.name: param
tags.text: date - Date or runtime-parseable string to inspect.

tags.name: param
tags.text: timeZone - Timezone used for clock extraction; defaults to TIME_ZONE_LOCAL.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Hour times 60 plus minute, from zero through 1439 for valid inputs; seconds are discarded.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: Propagates invalid-date or timezone errors from Intl.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
```ts
import { getMinutesFromMidnight } from '@alneas/appkit-core/data/date-utils';
console.log(getMinutesFromMidnight('2024-01-15T14:30:00Z', 'UTC')); // 870
```

symbols.name: getStartOfMonth
signatures: (date: any, timeZone?: string | undefined): Date
symbols.summary: Builds a first-of-month string from selected-zone parts, then resolves the observed day to midnight.

tags.name: param
tags.text: date - Date or runtime-parseable instant string supplying selected-zone year/month.

tags.name: param
tags.text: timeZone - Timezone for extraction and midnight resolution; defaults to TIME_ZONE_LOCAL.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: The Date produced by setTime for that generated date-only string.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: Propagates invalid-date, timezone or nonexistent-midnight errors from Intl/setTime.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text: The intermediate ISO date-only string is parsed as UTC. In zones behind UTC the result can be the preceding civil day rather than the intended month's first day.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
```ts
import { getStartOfMonth } from '@alneas/appkit-core/data/date-utils';
console.log(getStartOfMonth('2024-01-15T12:00:00Z', 'UTC').toISOString()); // '2024-01-01T00:00:00.000Z'
```

symbols.name: getStartOfQuarter
signatures: (date: any, timeZone?: string | undefined): Date
symbols.summary: Builds the selected calendar quarter's first date and resolves its observed target-zone day to midnight.

tags.name: param
tags.text: date - Date or runtime-parseable instant string supplying the selected-zone year/month.

tags.name: param
tags.text: timeZone - Timezone for extraction and midnight resolution; defaults to TIME_ZONE_LOCAL.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: The Date produced from the generated January/April/July/October first date through setTime.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: Propagates invalid-date, timezone or nonexistent-midnight errors.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text: The date-only intermediate is parsed as UTC. In zones behind UTC the result can be the preceding civil day, so this is not a general civil-quarter boundary API.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
```ts
import { getStartOfQuarter } from '@alneas/appkit-core/data/date-utils';
console.log(getStartOfQuarter('2024-05-15T12:00:00Z', 'UTC').toISOString()); // '2024-04-01T00:00:00.000Z'
```

symbols.name: getStartOfYear

symbols.name: isDateInRange
signatures: (date: any, start: any, end: any): boolean
symbols.summary: Checks whether an instant lies between two inclusive timestamp bounds.

tags.name: param
tags.text: date - Date or runtime-parseable instant string to test.

tags.name: param
tags.text: start - Inclusive lower timestamp bound.

tags.name: param
tags.text: end - Inclusive upper timestamp bound.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: True when start <= date <= end in epoch milliseconds; invalid dates or reversed bounds produce false.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text: This compares instants rather than calendar days; an end date parsed at midnight does not include the remainder of that day.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
```ts
import { isDateInRange } from '@alneas/appkit-core/data/date-utils';
console.log(isDateInRange('2024-01-15T12:00:00Z', '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z', '2024-01-31T23:59:59Z')); // true
```

symbols.name: parseLocalDate
signatures: (dateStr: string, timeZone?: string | undefined): Date
symbols.summary: Parses a string with Date and resets the observed target-zone calendar day to midnight.

tags.name: param
tags.text: dateStr - Date-constructor input, conventionally YYYY-MM-DD. Date-only ISO input is initially parsed as UTC, not as a target-zone civil date.

tags.name: param
tags.text: timeZone - Timezone for observed-day extraction and midnight resolution; defaults to TIME_ZONE_LOCAL.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: A new Date at the observed day's target-zone midnight, using setTime's overlap rules.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: Propagates invalid-date, timezone or nonexistent-midnight errors from setTime.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text: For zones behind UTC, a YYYY-MM-DD input can resolve to the previous civil day. This implementation must not be used as a general timezone-independent civil-date parser.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
```ts
import { parseLocalDate } from '@alneas/appkit-core/data/date-utils';
console.log(parseLocalDate('2024-01-15', 'UTC').toISOString()); // '2024-01-15T00:00:00.000Z'
```

symbols.name: setTime
signatures: (date: any, hour: number, minute?: number | undefined, second?: number | undefined, timeZone?: string | undefined): Date
symbols.summary: Selects an instant with the requested wall-clock time on the date observed in a selected timezone.

tags.name: param
tags.text: date - Date or runtime-parseable string providing the calendar day in the target timezone.

tags.name: param
tags.text: hour - Integer hour from zero through 23.

tags.name: param
tags.text: minute - Integer minute from zero through 59; defaults to zero.

tags.name: param
tags.text: second - Integer second from zero through 59; defaults to zero.

tags.name: param
tags.text: timeZone - Timezone for calendar extraction and wall-clock resolution; absent/empty values use TIME_ZONE_LOCAL.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: A new Date with millisecond zero. If the wall time occurs twice, the earlier matching instant is returned.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: For non-integer/out-of-range clock values, a timezone gap with no matching instant, or invalid Date/Intl timezone input.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text: Offsets are sampled around the requested wall date; this is not a general historical timezone-disambiguation API. Input Date objects are not mutated.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
```ts
import { setTime } from '@alneas/appkit-core/data/date-utils';
console.log(setTime('2024-01-15T12:00:00Z', 0, 0, 0, 'Asia/Tokyo').toISOString()); // '2024-01-14T15:00:00.000Z'
```

symbols.summary: Returns an existing Date by reference or parses a string with the JavaScript Date constructor.

tags.name: returns

symbols.name: toInputDate
signatures: (val: unknown): string
symbols.summary: Formats a value as a host-local HTML date-input string with a lexical fallback for unparseable date-shaped strings.

tags.name: param
tags.text: val - Date, Date-constructor-compatible value or other input. Falsy values, including numeric zero, yield an empty string.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: YYYY-MM-DD from host-local date parts, the first ten characters of an unparseable string starting with that pattern, or an empty string on other invalid/coercion failures.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text: This is not date validation: the lexical fallback can preserve impossible dates. A UTC string can display a different host-local day.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
```ts
import { toInputDate } from '@alneas/appkit-core/data/date-utils';
console.log(toInputDate(new Date(2024, 0, 15))); // '2024-01-15'
console.log(toInputDate(null)); // ''
```

symbols.name: toInputDateTime
signatures: (val: unknown): string
symbols.summary: Formats a value as a host-local HTML datetime-local string with a lexical fallback.

tags.name: param
tags.text: val - Date, Date-constructor-compatible value or other input. Falsy values, including numeric zero, yield an empty string.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm from host-local fields, the first sixteen characters of an unparseable string matching that prefix, or an empty string on other failures.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text: Seconds and timezone offsets are omitted. The prefix fallback does not validate actual calendar or clock ranges.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
```ts
import { toInputDateTime } from '@alneas/appkit-core/data/date-utils';
console.log(toInputDateTime(new Date(2024, 0, 15, 14, 30))); // '2024-01-15T14:30'
console.log(toInputDateTime(null)); // ''
```

tags.text:
Tool schemas are application-owned, synchronous JSON Schema draft-07 or 2020-12.

defaults and property removal disabled. The registered action validator still runs.
No schema, handler, permission or output type is inferred from a TypeScript type.

action was replaced during execution. Context lifetime checks are owned by the registry.

JSON schemas, arguments and projected outputs must be plain finite JSON data, at most
64 levels deep, 10000 nodes and 1000000 serialized characters per value.

symbols.summary:

it does not race the promise or unlock a handler that ignores cancellation. A handler
resolving after cancellation is recorded as succeeded with cancelRequested=true.

remain failures. Late progress updates are ignored. Observers cannot break execution.

handle server authorization, idempotency and uncertain commit outcomes themselves.

symbols.name: castValuesBySchema
signatures: (values: any, schema: JSONSchemaProperty, options?: SchemaCastOptions | undefined): any
symbols.summary:
Convert form values, separately from JSON Schema validation. Never adds defaults,
resolves $ref, selects composition branches, or coerces booleans/dates/null values.
Numeric empty strings become null for nullable numeric types, otherwise undefined.
Legacy numeric parsing intentionally accepts prefixes and truncates integers.
Mismatched object/array values and unconvertible strings are retained for validation.
Walks only own declared properties, prefixItems and items; unknown properties survive.
Does not mutate inputs. Throws beyond depth 64 or 10,000 visited values (including cycles).

symbols.name: createAjvValidator
signatures: (options?: AjvValidatorOptions | undefined): ((schema: object, data: unknown, overrides?: any) => { valid: boolean; errors: {}; rawErrors?: {} | undefined; }) & { ajv: any; }
symbols.summary: Creates a validator using Ajv.

tags.name: param
tags.text: options - Validation options.

tags.name: param
tags.text: options.locale - Error message locale ('ja' | 'en'). If omitted, Ajv default messages are used.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Validation execution function.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Automatically selects draft-07/2020-12 based on $schema; compiled functions are not shared across instances.
Do not mutate the schema object after compilation; pass a new object instead.
The returned `ajv` property is the instance for the default draft. When using addSchema/addKeyword, specify the draft explicitly.
The default path disables type coercion and does not insert defaults or remove
keys. Explicit ajvOptions can enable input mutation. Unknown x-* keywords are
not business validation rules merely because strict mode is disabled.
Compilation/configuration failures throw; invalid data returns valid: false.
Runtime compilation requires a host that permits AJV's generated functions.

symbols.name: generateZodSchema
signatures: (schema: JSONSchema): ZodObject<Readonly<{ [k: string]: $ZodType<unknown, unknown, $ZodTypeInternals<unknown, unknown>>; }>, $strip>
symbols.summary:
Generates a Zod validation schema from a JSONSchema.

Produces appropriate Zod validators according to property type/format,
applying implemented JSON Schema constraints and supported x-zod extensions.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Partial conversion, not a JSON Schema evaluator. additionalProperties, type
unions and positive multipleOf are supported. Exclusive bounds, composition,
references and advanced array constraints are not generally preserved. format: date only
checks string type. Use createAjvValidator at the authoritative JSON boundary.
Only implemented x-zod options take effect; declarations do not imply support.
Root/nested required entries are checked even without properties declarations;
enum applies at the root as well as to nested values.
Declared/required __proto__ properties are rejected at conversion time.

tags.name: param
tags.text: schema - JSONSchema schema

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Zod object schema

tags.name: example

symbols.name: generateZodSchemaCode
signatures: (schema: JSONSchema): string
symbols.summary: Serializes a JSON Schema into a module that calls generateZodSchema at runtime.

tags.name: param
tags.text:
schema - JSON-serializable schema; title, then x-db.tableName, then
"unnamed" supplies the export-name prefix. Non-identifier characters become
underscores and a leading digit receives an underscore prefix.

tags.name: returns
tags.text:
Module source importing generateZodSchema from "./compiler.js" and exporting
the named schema by passing JSON.parse of the serialized input to that helper.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: Throws if JSON serialization fails, for example for cyclic input or BigInt.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
The output is not a standalone z.object expression and this function does not
validate or compile the schema. Evaluating the emitted module runs the helper
and can raise its schema-conversion errors. Provide a sibling compiler module
exporting generateZodSchema and a resolver that supports the emitted extensionless
import; native Node.js ESM does not resolve that import without adjustment.
The runtime helper uses Zod, which is a Core dependency.

tags.name: example

symbols.name: generateZodSchema
signatures: (schema: JSONSchema): ZodObject<Readonly<{ [k: string]: $ZodType<unknown, unknown, $ZodTypeInternals<unknown, unknown>>; }>, $strip>
symbols.summary:
Generates a Zod validation schema from a JSONSchema.

Produces appropriate Zod validators according to property type/format,
applying implemented JSON Schema constraints and supported x-zod extensions.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Partial conversion, not a JSON Schema evaluator. additionalProperties, type
unions and positive multipleOf are supported. Exclusive bounds, composition,
references and advanced array constraints are not generally preserved. format: date only
checks string type. Use createAjvValidator at the authoritative JSON boundary.
Only implemented x-zod options take effect; declarations do not imply support.
Root/nested required entries are checked even without properties declarations;
enum applies at the root as well as to nested values.
Declared/required __proto__ properties are rejected at conversion time.

tags.name: param
tags.text: schema - JSONSchema schema

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Zod object schema

tags.name: example

symbols.name: generateZodSchemaCode
signatures: (schema: JSONSchema): string
symbols.summary: Serializes a JSON Schema into a module that calls generateZodSchema at runtime.

tags.name: param
tags.text:
schema - JSON-serializable schema; title, then x-db.tableName, then
"unnamed" supplies the export-name prefix. Non-identifier characters become
underscores and a leading digit receives an underscore prefix.

tags.name: returns
tags.text:
Module source importing generateZodSchema from "./compiler.js" and exporting
the named schema by passing JSON.parse of the serialized input to that helper.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: Throws if JSON serialization fails, for example for cyclic input or BigInt.

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
The output is not a standalone z.object expression and this function does not
validate or compile the schema. Evaluating the emitted module runs the helper
and can raise its schema-conversion errors. Provide a sibling compiler module
exporting generateZodSchema and a resolver that supports the emitted extensionless
import; native Node.js ESM does not resolve that import without adjustment.
The runtime helper uses Zod, which is a Core dependency.

symbols.name: createAjvValidator
signatures: (options?: AjvValidatorOptions | undefined): ((schema: object, data: unknown, overrides?: any) => { valid: boolean; errors: {}; rawErrors?: {} | undefined; }) & { ajv: any; }

tags.name: remarks
tags.text:
Automatically selects draft-07/2020-12 based on $schema; compiled functions are not shared across instances.
Do not mutate the schema object after compilation; pass a new object instead.
The returned `ajv` property is the instance for the default draft. When using addSchema/addKeyword, specify the draft explicitly.
The default path disables type coercion and does not insert defaults or remove
keys. Explicit ajvOptions can enable input mutation. Unknown x-* keywords are
not business validation rules merely because strict mode is disabled.
Compilation/configuration failures throw; invalid data returns valid: false.
Runtime compilation requires a host that permits AJV's generated functions.

symbols.summary: Compiles supported filters and CRUD operations to parameterized PostgreSQL SQL. The host owns credentials, schema, permissions and connection lifetime. Identifier/value validation limits query syntax but does not establish authorization.

tags.name: remarks

symbols.name: ContainedPathRoot
symbols.summary:
Pins a trusted root (including a not-yet-created root) to an absolute physical
path. Every operation rejects symlinks in that path and below it, including
dangling links. An initial root alias is resolved once at construction.

This is server-only. The root and its ancestors must not be concurrently
renamed or modified by untrusted OS users: portable Node path APIs cannot
provide an atomic openat-style directory walk. Hard links are also outside
this boundary; provision an application-owned directory with suitable ACLs.

QueryOptions are requests rather than guarantees across every backend. Generic
result types describe the caller's expected shape and do not validate responses.
Operations can reject with backend/transport failures; cancellation and retry
policies are implementation-specific and do not imply transaction rollback.

signatures: export type Filter = Record<string, unknown>;

Filter criteria for record retrieval.

These are common filter conventions; supported operators and value semantics
are adapter-specific and are validated by that adapter:
- `$eq` (eq): Equals
- `$neq` (neq): Not equals
- `$lt` (lt), `$lte` (lte): Less than / Less than or equal to
- `$gt` (gt), `$gte` (gte): Greater than / Greater than or equal to
- `$in` (in): Included in array
- `$nin` (nin): Not included in array
- `$regex`: Regular expression match

symbols.name: planGanttTasks
signatures: <T extends GanttPlanningTask>(tasks: {}, dependencies: {}, options?: GanttSchedulingOptions | undefined): GanttScheduleResult<T>
symbols.summary:
Plan whole working days with a shared calendar and optional resource capacities.
Dates must be local midnight (date-only strings are parsed locally). Finishes are
exclusive next-working-day boundaries. A positive span with no working days gets
one day; durationDays overrides inferred duration, including zero-day milestones.

Stable topological/input order decides resource precedence. Tasks are never split,
pulled before their input starts, or optimized for shortest makespan. All statuses
participate; actual/frozen work and individual resource calendars are not modeled.
Summary rows are preserved but excluded from planning. Invalid inputs, cycles,
over-capacity demand and exhausted search bounds throw without mutating inputs.
CPM is dependency-only BEFORE leveling; capacity delays are reported separately.

tags.name: param
tags.text: tasks - Task records with unique IDs and release dates; inputs are not mutated.

tags.name: param
tags.text: dependencies - Unique directed leaf-task links using FS/SS/FF/SF and integer lagDays.

tags.name: param
tags.text: options - Optional working calendar, resource leveling and search bounds; defaults to {} for the planner. Omitting it from scheduleGanttTasks preserves legacy calendar-day/time-of-day behavior.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Scheduled tasks, dependency-only CPM, capacity delays and project finish; empty leaf input has empty diagnostics and null finish.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: Throws invalid graph/date/calendar/duration inputs or exhausted search bounds; the working-day planner also rejects infeasible resource demand.

tags.name: typeParam
tags.text: T - Consumer task shape extending the required scheduling fields; extra fields are preserved.

symbols.summary:

tags.text: Throws invalid graph/date/calendar/duration inputs or exhausted search bounds; the working-day planner also rejects infeasible resource demand.

Apply FS/SS/FF/SF constraints in topological order, moving successors forward only.
Preserves each task's calendar-day duration and time-of-day using local date arithmetic.
Input tasks/links are not mutated. Cycles, missing IDs and summary dependencies throw.
A third options argument opts into the local-midnight day planner with working calendars
and optional capacity leveling. Omit it to preserve legacy time-of-day behavior.

tags.name: param
tags.text: tasks - Task records with unique IDs and release dates; inputs are not mutated.

tags.name: param
tags.text: dependencies - Unique directed leaf-task links using FS/SS/FF/SF and integer lagDays.

tags.name: param
tags.text: options - Optional working calendar, resource leveling and search bounds; defaults to {} for the planner. Omitting it from scheduleGanttTasks preserves legacy calendar-day/time-of-day behavior.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Tasks in input order with scheduled dates; unchanged tasks may retain original references.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: Throws invalid graph/date/calendar/duration inputs or exhausted search bounds; the working-day planner also rejects infeasible resource demand.

tags.name: typeParam
tags.text: T - Consumer task shape extending the required scheduling fields; extra fields are preserved.

symbols.summary:
Resolves the label (typically family name) to display on a fallback seal.

Priority order:
1. `options.sealLabel`
2. `options.familyName`

When `nameOrder: "auto"`:
- Names containing CJK characters: use first token
- 2 or more Latin words: use last token
- Otherwise: use first token

Serializes the represented UBL 2.1 Invoice, CreditNote, Order and DespatchAdvice fields.

symbols.name: getCalculatedJapaneseHolidays
signatures: (year: number, equinoxDays?: JapaneseEquinoxDays | undefined): {}
symbols.summary:
Calculates Japanese holidays under the ordinary rules in effect from 2022.
Includes fixed dates, Happy Monday rules, Sunday substitutes and citizens' holidays.
Equinox defaults use a linear/leap-year approximation, not an astronomical ephemeris
or official announcement. Supply announced days when official dates are required.
Excludes historical special moves (including 2020/2021) and future one-off laws.

tags.name: param
tags.text: year Integer, 2022–2099; unsupported years throw RangeError.

tags.name: param
tags.text: equinoxDays Optional announced March/September days, each 19–24.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Fresh sorted holiday records. Predicted dates require official verification.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
import { getCalculatedJapaneseHolidays } from '@alneas/appkit-core/japan/holidays/calculated';
getCalculatedJapaneseHolidays(2026).some(day => day.date === '2026-09-22'); // true

tags.name: throws
tags.text: RangeError for years outside 2022–2099 or equinox days outside the integer range 19–24.

symbols.name: addDays
signatures: (date: any, days: number): Date
symbols.summary: Adds multiples of a fixed 24-hour duration to an instant.

tags.name: param
tags.text: date - Date or runtime-parseable string providing the starting instant.

tags.name: param
tags.text: days - Number of 86,400,000-millisecond periods to add; negative and fractional values are accepted.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: A new Date from elapsed-millisecond arithmetic; invalid/non-finite inputs produce an invalid Date.

tags.name: remarks

```ts
import { addDays } from '@alneas/appkit-core/data/date-utils';
console.log(addDays('2024-01-15T00:00:00Z', 7).toISOString()); // '2024-01-22T00:00:00.000Z'
```

symbols.name: compareTimes

symbols.summary: Compares two colon-separated clock strings after converting their first two fields to numbers.

tags.name: param
tags.text: time2 - Second clock string, conventionally HH:mm.

symbols.name: ContainedPathRoot
symbols.summary:
Pins a trusted root (including a not-yet-created root) to an absolute physical
path. Every operation rejects symlinks in that path and below it, including
dangling links. An initial root alias is resolved once at construction.

This is server-only. The root and its ancestors must not be concurrently
renamed or modified by untrusted OS users: portable Node path APIs cannot
provide an atomic openat-style directory walk. Hard links are also outside
this boundary; provision an application-owned directory with suitable ACLs.

symbols.name: LocalStorageAdapter
symbols.summary:
Storage adapter for the local filesystem.

Used to store files on the local disk instead of cloud storage
during development and testing.

## Features
- Uses Node.js `fs/promises`
- Automatic directory creation
- Automatic MIME type detection
- Recursive file listing

Keys must be relative paths without dot segments or backslashes. Symlinks
below the pinned root are rejected. The directory and its ancestors must be
owned by the application and protected from concurrent untrusted mutation.

symbols.name: formatUSDate
signatures: (date: Date, timeZone: string): string
symbols.summary:
Formats an instant as an en-US numeric date in an explicitly selected timezone.
The United States has multiple timezones; this API has no host-local default.

tags.name: param
tags.text: date Valid Date representing an instant; civil date strings are not accepted.

tags.name: param
tags.text: timeZone Intl timezone identifier, for example America/New_York or UTC.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Month/day/year text in the supplied timezone.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: RangeError for an invalid Date or timezone; TypeError if timezone is absent.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
import { formatUSDate } from '@alneas/appkit-core/us/format';
formatUSDate(new Date('2026-07-04T02:00:00Z'), 'America/New_York'); // '7/3/2026'

symbols.name: getUSFederalHolidays
signatures: (year: number, options?: USFederalHolidayOptions | undefined): {}
symbols.summary:
Lists the eleven recurring nationwide federal holidays under the current rules.
Observed mode (default) moves Saturday to Friday and Sunday to Monday for a
standard Monday–Friday schedule. Results are filtered by selected date, including
next January's New Year's Day when observed in December of the requested year.
Excludes state/local holidays, Inauguration Day and one-off executive closures.
Additional dates are used exactly as supplied and replace labels on matching
selected dates. Exclusions run last. No remote data is fetched.
This is a planning policy, not a private-employer working-day determination.
Source: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/federal-holidays/

tags.name: param
tags.text: year Calendar year from 2021 through 2099. Future rules can change.

tags.name: param
tags.text: options Observance mode plus explicit additional or excluded closure dates; defaults to {}.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Fresh date-sorted records whose selected date falls within year.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: RangeError for unsupported years or invalid override dates; TypeError for unnamed additions.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
import { getUSFederalHolidays } from '@alneas/appkit-core/us/holidays';
getUSFederalHolidays(2026).find(day => day.actualDate === '2026-07-04')?.date; // '2026-07-03'

tags.name: remarks
tags.text: Omitted options default to {}: observed=true with no added or excluded dates.

symbols.name: usFederalHolidayCalendar
signatures: ({ year, month, day }: USCalendarDate): boolean
symbols.summary:
Tests a civil date against the standard observed federal holiday calendar.
Structurally compatible with data-engine's HolidayCalendar; no engine dependency.

tags.name: param
tags.text: parts Civil date with zero-based month; the caller converts instants to its timezone.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Whether the civil date is an observed federal holiday.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: RangeError for an invalid civil date or year outside 2021–2099.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
import { usFederalHolidayCalendar } from '@alneas/appkit-core/us';
usFederalHolidayCalendar({ year: 2026, month: 6, day: 3 }); // true

symbols.name: createUSBusinessDocument
signatures: (input: USBusinessDocumentInput): USBusinessDocumentModel
symbols.summary:
Assembles a USD quote, invoice or credit-note model using generic engine calculation.
A host owns rendering/export, fonts and safe text handling; no PDF library is loaded.
Supply precomputed line amounts and explicit tax/rounding policy. Uses JavaScript
numbers, not exact decimal accounting or automatic tax determination. Credit notes
use positive magnitudes and require an original invoice reference; ledger signs
remain caller-owned. Civil due dates are never shifted by a holiday calendar.

tags.name: param

tags.name: returns

symbols.summary:
Creates a civil-date provider using a snapshot of application calendar overrides.
Use this for announced one-off closures or company policy without changing the
built-in federal rules. No external service is polled and no announcement is inferred.

tags.name: param
tags.text: options Observance mode, added closures and excluded dates; exclusions win; defaults to {}.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: A structurally compatible data-engine HolidayCalendar; months are zero-based.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: RangeError for invalid override dates; TypeError for unnamed additions.

tags.name: example
remarks

symbols.name: getUSFederalHolidays
signatures: (year: number, options?: USFederalHolidayOptions | undefined): {}
symbols.summary:
Lists the eleven recurring nationwide federal holidays under the current rules.
Observed mode (default) moves Saturday to Friday and Sunday to Monday for a
standard Monday–Friday schedule. Results are filtered by selected date, including
next January's New Year's Day when observed in December of the requested year.
Excludes state/local holidays, Inauguration Day and one-off executive closures.
Additional dates are used exactly as supplied and replace labels on matching
selected dates. Exclusions run last. No remote data is fetched.
This is a planning policy, not a private-employer working-day determination.
Source: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/federal-holidays/

tags.name: param
tags.text: year Calendar year from 2021 through 2099. Future rules can change.

tags.name: param
tags.text: options Observance mode plus explicit additional or excluded closure dates; defaults to {}.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Fresh date-sorted records whose selected date falls within year.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: RangeError for unsupported years or invalid override dates; TypeError for unnamed additions.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
import { getUSFederalHolidays } from '@alneas/appkit-core/us/holidays';
getUSFederalHolidays(2026).find(day => day.actualDate === '2026-07-04')?.date; // '2026-07-03'

tags.name: remarks
tags.text: Omitted options default to {}: observed=true with no added or excluded dates.

symbols.name: usFederalHolidayCalendar
signatures: ({ year, month, day }: USCalendarDate): boolean
symbols.summary:
Tests a civil date against the standard observed federal holiday calendar.
Structurally compatible with data-engine's HolidayCalendar; no engine dependency.

tags.name: param
tags.text: parts Civil date with zero-based month; the caller converts instants to its timezone.

tags.name: returns
tags.text: Whether the civil date is an observed federal holiday.

tags.name: throws
tags.text: RangeError for an invalid civil date or year outside 2021–2099.

tags.name: example
tags.text:
import { usFederalHolidayCalendar } from '@alneas/appkit-core/us';
usFederalHolidayCalendar({ year: 2026, month: 6, day: 3 }); // true
